transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's
asking the European Union for more support going into winter.
Terry Schultz reports the EU backup is all the more important, as Zelensky's ties with
President Trump increasingly fray.
President Zelensky said he's counting on the EU for more assistance, as his relationship
with the Trump administration deteriorates.
Russia continues to attack Ukraine's energy infrastructure, and winter approaches.
It's not only energy, it's also air defense and funding, and I'm thankful that EU stands
with us.
Some EU leaders are reportedly pressing Zelensky to rein in his criticism of Trump, but they're
also concerned the U.S. ended its ban on Russian diesel imports, earning Moscow money.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
We will not lift any sanctions unless Russia stops the war.
EU leaders are again debating whether and how almost $250 billion worth of frozen Russian
assets can be used to fund Ukraine.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
Democrats believe they can flip a Florida congressional seat.
Republicans have control since 2020, and P.R.'s Claudia Garzales reports the race in Miami
will test President Trump's support among Latino voters.
Florida Republican Maria Elvira Salazar says she does not regret telling President Trump
that he's "gone too far" on immigration.
Salazar told NPR during a Miami event Thursday she talked with Trump after her TV ad last
month, warning those policies were driving Latinos away.
And I told him, you know what I'm telling you is what my people are feeling.
But you know, this is democracy, where we tell the boss, hey, this is what's happening
on my neck of the woods.
The three-term Congresswoman is locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Elliot
Rodriguez, who like Salazar is an ex-broadcast journalist with Cuban roots.
Early voting starts Monday in the Latino majority district.
Claudia Garzales, NPR News.
Officials in Southern California are preparing for wildfires.
Much of the region is under a red flag warning today.
From member station LAist Lucas Brady Woods has more.
The risk is so high right now because of a mix of strong winds, dry vegetation and low
humidity.
If a fire breaks out under these conditions, it can easily spread out of control.
Similar factors drove the deadly Los Angeles wildfires in 2025.
Los Angeles Fire Department Captain Milo Cope says wind can spread embers over long distances.
They can fly up to a mile out and then drop down.
And because the weather is dry, they drop down and they catch and they'll light that
brush on fire ahead of us.
California Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass have ordered extra firefighting
resources to high-risk areas across the region.
For NPR News, I'm Lucas Brady Woods in Los Angeles.
On Wall Street, stocks are mixed.
The Dow is up 240 points.
The NASDAQ is down 200.
This is NPR.
Authorities in Bend, Oregon say three children and a teacher were killed yesterday in a school
shooting.
Authorities in Bend say the shooter was a 16-year-old male.
He was shot and killed by a bystander.
A study finds that ultra-processed foods overall do not increase a person's risk of developing
colorectal cancer.
But NPR's Maria Godoy reports the risk varied depending on the type of food.
The majority of industrially made packaged foods sold in grocery stores count as ultra-processed,
from jarred pasta sauces to sugary drinks.
In this study, researchers looked at data from more than 460,000 U.S. adults between
the ages of 50 and 71 over nearly two decades.
They found that eating processed meats was linked to a higher risk of colorectal cancer.
But a higher intake of other foods from the ultra-process category, specifically whole
grains and dairy, was associated with a lower risk.
The researchers say the findings support current recommendations to consume whole grains, fiber,
dairy, and calcium, and avoid processed meats.
The findings appear in the journal Plus Medicine.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
The Milwaukee Brewers are going to their first World Series since 1982.
They sweat the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games, beating them 6-4 last night.
They'll face the winner of the American League Championship Series.
Cleveland leads Tampa Bay in that series, two games to one.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
